title: Bellingham’s Extra-Time Heroics Send England Past Norway in a Scorcher
summary: Imagine playing soccer when it’s 108 degrees outside! That’s what England and Norway faced in their World Cup quarterfinal on Saturday in Miami Gardens, Florida. The heat was so intense that players looked slower and passes weren’t as sharp. But the game was still full of drama. Norway struck first. In the 36th minute, Andreas Schjelderup fired a left-footed shot past England’s goalkeeper to make it 1-0. It was the fifth time Norway scored first in this tournament. England didn’t wait long to answer. Just before halftime, Jude Bellingham — the same player who saved England in the last round — scored to tie the game 1-1. In the second half, Norway thought they scored again, but the goal was canceled after a video review showed a push by Erling Haaland. The game went to extra time, and Bellingham struck again just three minutes in. He pounced on a rebound and slotted the ball into the net for his sixth goal of the tournament. Norway complained that the ball hit a sky cam wire before the goal, but FIFA said there was no evidence. England held on to win 2-1. It was Norway’s best-ever World Cup run, but England moves on. Next up: a huge semifinal against Argentina on Wednesday in Atlanta. Can England win their first World Cup since 1966? Stay tuned!
why_it_matters: Just like in school sports on a scorching day, this match shows that you have to push through discomfort and stay focused to succeed, especially when every little mistake can change the outcome.

background_read: England won the World Cup only once, back in 1966, and fans have waited a very long time for another trophy. Norway had never gone this far in a World Cup before; getting to the quarterfinals was already their best result ever. The game was played in Miami Gardens, Florida, where summer temperatures can often climb above 100 degrees Fahrenheit, making it extremely tough for players to run for 90 minutes.
Article_Structure: WHO: Jude Bellingham, Andreas Schjelderup, Erling Haaland, England goalkeeper
WHAT: England came from behind to beat Norway 2-1 in extra time, with Bellingham scoring twice.
WHERE: Miami Gardens, Florida, in an outdoor stadium with extreme heat.
WHY: Norway's second goal was disallowed after video review for a push, and then Bellingham's extra-time goal decided the match, helping England advance.

perspectives.description: Fans are overjoyed that their young star Bellingham keeps rescuing the team. They believe this might finally be the year their long wait for a World Cup ends.
Supporters feel proud that their team played so well in their best-ever World Cup run, but they are heartbroken that a disallowed goal and a late extra-time goal ended their dream.
Some people worry that playing in such extreme heat is dangerous for athletes and question whether matches should be scheduled at cooler times of day.
